fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Composite resin veneers offer a conservative way to improve the shape, colour and proportions of your teeth. Because they are built up and sculpted directly onto your teeth, treatment is often completed in a single appointment, and in many cases little or no enamel needs to be removed.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: At Precision Dental, we take the time to understand what you would like to change and whether composite veneers suit your teeth, bite and lifestyle.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are Composite Resin Veneers?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite resin is a tooth-coloured material that is also used for white fillings. When used as a veneer, it is applied in layers to the front of the tooth, shaped by hand and polished to a smooth finish. Shades can be blended to suit your surrounding teeth.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Compared with porcelain veneers, composite veneers usually involve less tooth preparation, are completed more quickly and can be repaired more easily if they chip. However, composite is more prone to staining and wear over time, so it typically needs more maintenance, polishing and eventual replacement.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Are Composite Resin Veneers Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite veneers may be considered if you have:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Small chips or worn edges on your front teeth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Minor gaps between teeth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Teeth that are slightly uneven in shape or length

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Localised discolouration that does not respond to whitening

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A preference for a conservative, reversible or budget-conscious option

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite veneers work best when your teeth and gums are healthy. If you grind your teeth, bite your nails or have significant crowding, we will discuss whether another approach may be more suitable. If you are also considering teeth whitening, we recommend whitening first, as composite does not change colour with whitening treatment.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Consultation

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We begin with an examination of your teeth, gums and bite, along with photographs and digital X-rays where needed. We talk about your goals, explain the benefits and limitations of composite veneers and provide a clear quote.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Treatment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: On the day of treatment, the tooth surface is cleaned and lightly prepared. Where needed, local anaesthetic is used to keep you comfortable, although many patients do not require it. The composite resin is applied in thin layers, each one shaped and set with a curing light. Once the shape is complete, the veneers are refined and polished.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Review

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Before you leave, we check your bite and the appearance of your veneers with you. A short review appointment may be recommended to make any fine adjustments.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Brush twice daily with a soft toothbrush and non-abrasive toothpaste, and clean between your teeth each day. Limit highly staining foods and drinks, such as coffee, tea and red wine, and rinse with water afterwards. Avoid biting hard objects, and consider a custom mouthguard for contact sport. Regular check-ups and cleans allow us to polish and maintain your veneers.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Composite Veneers

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Composite Veneers

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite veneers rely on careful hands and an eye for detail. Dr Billy Choi takes a thoughtful approach to shade selection and shaping, and he will always discuss alternatives, including whitening and porcelain veneers, so you can choose the option that suits you.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How long do composite veneers last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite veneers can last several years with good care, although their lifespan varies. They may need polishing, repair or replacement over time due to staining or wear.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Do composite veneers damage my teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite veneers usually require minimal preparation of the natural tooth. In some cases, a small amount of enamel is shaped to improve the result, and we will explain this before treatment.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can composite veneers be repaired?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. If a composite veneer chips, it can often be repaired directly in the chair without replacing the whole veneer.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will composite veneers stain?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite resin is more prone to staining than porcelain. Regular professional polishing and limiting staining foods and drinks can help maintain their appearance.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How many appointments will I need?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most patients need a consultation followed by one treatment appointment. A short review may be suggested afterwards.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Are composite veneers covered by health funds?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Some extras policies provide rebates for cosmetic or restorative items. We can provide item numbers so you can check with your fund, and claims are processed on the spot through HICAPS.
